templates.name: Designer
templates.description: Interviews you to capture product truth, then designs, quality-checks, and publishes a complete static site into the Front of House preview.

templates.name: Ledger Implementer
templates.description: The team’s product engineer. Turn ledger specifications into working changes in the project repository. Use GitHub for code and the ledger for work state. Keep one branch and one PR per item. Delegate browser QA to the qa subagent and independent code review to reviewer; record their findings against the exact head SHA.

templates.name: Ledger Infra
templates.description: The team’s infrastructure engineer. Own cloud resources, CI, credentials and deployment configuration. Discover the target product and conventions through the ledger; work through the installed Cloudflare and GitHub tools. Record provisioning results on the item.

templates.name: Ledger Intake
templates.description: The team’s front of house. Turn requests into testable specifications, break large plans into reviewable work, and relay human decisions. Read project context through the ledger. Report pending May I approvals to the named human and report when their work is live.

templates.name: Vercel Issuer
templates.description: The team's Vercel platform engineer: creates Vercel projects and mints project-scoped tokens for teammates behind a human approval gate. Holds the one full-account token; every privileged operation shows the human the exact request and justification before it runs.

templates.name: Cloudflare
templates.description: Cloudflare product selection, provisioning, development and deployment skills with harnesst credential integration.

templates.name: GitHub
templates.description: Everything an agent needs to work GitHub as itself: the GitHub App channel (its @mention identity and credentials), the gh CLI in its sandbox, and the skill that turns the App's private key into a working token.

templates.name: Google Sheets
templates.description: Everything an agent needs to work with Google Sheets: the connector (install → Connect Google → read/write spreadsheets) plus a usage skill teaching A1 notation, read-before-write, the values vs batchUpdate operations, and how to handle transient Google outages. Recommended way to add Sheets.

templates.name: Ledger
templates.description: A shared work ledger with authenticated wakes, evidence and human approval gates.

templates.name: Vercel
templates.description: Everything an agent needs to deploy to Vercel safely: the gated Vercel CLI tool (project-scoped token, human approval by default) plus the deploying skill that teaches the provisioning and deploy flow. Recommended way to make an agent a Vercel deployer.

templates.name: Discord
templates.description: Talk to this agent from Discord — one-click connect via harnesst's shared Discord app, a slash command named after the agent, and signature-verified interactions via eve's discordChannel.

templates.name: GitHub
templates.description: Talk to this agent by @mentioning it in GitHub issue and pull-request comments — a GitHub App with webhook signature verification via eve's githubChannel.

templates.name: Ledger wake
templates.description: Authenticated, claimed ledger delivery starts one agent turn per live lease.

templates.name: AgentMail
templates.description: Read and label mail in an AgentMail inbox (agentmail.to) with a user-supplied API key — no OAuth. Ships four tools: list the account's inboxes, list/search messages by date range, labels (e.g. unread), sender, or subject, read a full message including attachment downloads (invoice PDFs are the point), and add/remove labels. Read + label only by design: nothing shipped here can send, delete, or provision mail — the billing-inbox rule, enforced by omission.

templates.name: Gmail
templates.description: Read, label, and send mail from the connected Google account. One template, selectable permission levels: pick Read mail / Manage labels / Send mail at install (read-only by default), connect the mailbox on the agent's Deployment tab, and the agent gets gmail__* tools via eve's OpenAPI connection — access tokens self-refresh at runtime, and the granted level is visible to the agent so it never promises what it can't do.

templates.name: Google Sheets
templates.description: Read and write Google Sheets from this agent. Install it, then click Connect Google on the agent's Deployment tab to authorize your account, and the agent gets google_sheets__* tools (read/append/update cells, metadata, batch updates) via eve's OpenAPI connection — access tokens self-refresh at runtime.

templates.name: May I?
templates.description: Human approvals for agent actions via May I? (mayi.sh). Install it, click Connect on the agent's Deployment tab (harnesst registers the OAuth client automatically — no operator app to create), and gated tools park until a human approves in the May I? app, then resume with a signed receipt. Scheduled work that may need an approval must use the handler form of an eve schedule and hand the run to the channel with receive(mayi, ...) — task-mode schedules can't park for a human.

templates.name: Xero
templates.description: Bookkeeping operations against a Xero organisation through harnesst's brokered-capability framework: the agent's container never holds any Xero credential. harnesst keeps the OAuth grant and executes only a whitelisted set of operations — read reference data, search bills, look up and create contacts, and create DRAFT bills (a human approves them in Xero) with attached source files. Which operation groups are enabled is your choice at install time and editable any time from the Deployment tab, with instant effect.

templates.name: Agent Browser
templates.description: Browser automation with the agent-browser CLI: navigate pages, inspect accessibility snapshots, click/fill by refs, capture screenshots, and run web QA from the sandbox shell.

templates.name: Agents Sdk
templates.description: Build, debug, or review Cloudflare Agents SDK applications using the agents package.

templates.name: Breaking Down Work
templates.description: Use when an agreed request needs several independently reviewable changes, infrastructure dependencies, or proposed child items for plan approval.

templates.name: Building Cloudflare apps
templates.description: How to build a full-stack web app on Cloudflare Workers — a React + Vite SPA with a Worker API backend: choosing the scaffold, project layout, wrangler.jsonc semantics, the SPA-vs-Worker routing rules, the verify workflow, and bindings. Building only; deploying and shipping to a forge are separate skills.

templates.name: Clarifying A Request
templates.description: Use when a person requests a build, change or fix that is not yet a testable specification, or challenges an existing spec.

templates.name: Cloudflare
templates.description: Discover and choose Cloudflare products for apps, APIs, AI agents, storage, networking, and security. Use for architecture and product selection, including when the user describes a need without naming a Cloudflare product; then find the relevant skill or documentation.

templates.name: Cloudflare Email Service
templates.description: Implement or troubleshoot Cloudflare Email Sending and Email Routing integrations and their delivery configuration.

templates.name: Cloudflare One
templates.description: Design, configure, troubleshoot, or review Cloudflare One Zero Trust and SASE deployments. Use cloudflare-one-migrations for migration planning from other vendors.

templates.name: Cloudflare One Migrations
templates.description: Assess and plan migrations from existing VPN, SWG, or SASE platforms to Cloudflare One, including policy mapping, parity gaps, and rollout.

templates.name: Deploying Cloudflare apps
templates.description: How to deploy an app to Cloudflare and provision what it needs — wrangler config and deploys, KV/D1/R2/Queues/Pages, dry-runs, and getting deploy credentials into a CI pipeline. Cloudflare only; getting the code and wiring a specific forge's pipeline are separate skills.

templates.name: Deploying Vercel apps
templates.description: How to take an app to production on Vercel through the gated Vercel CLI tool: getting a project provisioned by the platform teammate, deploying, configuring env, connecting git, and verifying before mutating.

templates.name: Developer toolchain
templates.description: A broad developer toolchain preinstalled in the agent's sandbox — git, gh, jq, ripgrep, build tools, python3, pnpm/yarn, and friends — plus a skill inventorying what's there. A deliberate superset: install once, stop apt-getting per session.

templates.name: Durable Objects
templates.description: Build, debug, or review Cloudflare Durable Objects code for persistent state and coordination.

templates.name: GitHub App auth
templates.description: Exchange the agent's GitHub App private key for a short-lived installation token (GH_TOKEN) and commit as the App's bot identity, with gh and git preinstalled in the sandbox — the credential mechanics every GitHub-using agent needs, and nothing else.

templates.name: Google Sheets usage
templates.description: Practical guidance for driving the google_sheets__* tools: A1 notation, read-before-write discipline, RAW vs USER_ENTERED, append vs update, the batchUpdate request shapes for structural changes, and how to handle transient 429/5xx failures without reporting them as empty results.

templates.name: Authoring eve agents with harnesst MCP
templates.description: End-to-end guidance for authoring eve agents through harnesst's MCP server: save complete files, review every pending change, publish once, and poll every deployment until live.

templates.name: Impeccable
templates.description: A comprehensive frontend design skill for creating, critiquing, refining, and quality-checking polished interfaces inside harnesst/eve agents.

templates.name: Nextjs On Cloudflare
templates.description: Build, migrate, and deploy Next.js apps on Cloudflare Workers with vinext. Use when starting a Next.js project on Cloudflare, moving an existing app to Workers, choosing between vinext and OpenNext, or setting up vinext for Workers. For setup, migration, or deployment, install vinext's upstream skills with `npx skills add cloudflare/vinext` if missing, then read and follow the applicable skill and docs.

templates.name: Reviewing a pull request
templates.description: Two-axis PR review from a local checkout — standards (repo conventions plus a code-smell baseline) and spec (does it do what the issue asked) — delivered as one ranked review.

templates.name: Sandbox Migrate To Next
templates.description: Migrate Cloudflare Sandbox apps from stable @cloudflare/sandbox to @cloudflare/sandbox@next (SDK 1.0 preview). Use sandbox-next for apps already on the preview.

templates.name: Sandbox Next
templates.description: Build or maintain Cloudflare Sandbox apps on @cloudflare/sandbox@next (SDK 1.0 preview). Use sandbox-migrate-to-next when porting a stable app.

templates.name: Sandbox Stable
templates.description: Build or maintain Cloudflare Sandbox apps on the stable @cloudflare/sandbox package. Use sandbox-next for preview apps and sandbox-migrate-to-next for stable-to-preview migrations.

templates.name: Turnstile Spin
templates.description: Set up, repair, or migrate to Cloudflare Turnstile bot verification in an existing frontend and backend, including server-side Siteverify.

templates.name: Using The Ledger
templates.description: Use when a ledger wake arrives or before recording evidence, handing code to infra for a preview, moving work, resolving a block, or relaying human approval.

templates.name: Web Perf
templates.description: Audit, diagnose, or optimize website loading and interaction performance, Core Web Vitals, and Lighthouse performance scores.

templates.name: Workers Best Practices
templates.description: Cloudflare Workers best practices for production applications. Use when writing, reviewing, or configuring Workers.

templates.name: Wrangler
templates.description: Run or troubleshoot Wrangler CLI commands and configure Worker projects for local development, deployment, and Cloudflare resource management.

templates.name: Asset Library
templates.description: Store and retrieve durable, versioned files shared by every agent in this repository. Assets are committed under assets/ on the managed branch without exposing GitHub credentials to agents.

templates.name: Discord Send Message
templates.description: Send a message to a Discord channel by channel id via harnesst's control plane, using the installation's shared Discord app — scoped to servers this agent is connected to.

templates.name: Extract PDF Text
templates.description: Extract embedded text from a PDF staged under /workspace/home, without uploading the document or requiring a secret. Base64 remains available for compatibility, but local path handoff keeps file bytes out of model context. Returns text and page count with bounded input and output; scanned or image-only PDFs are reported clearly because this tool does not perform OCR.

templates.name: Web Search
templates.description: Search and research the live web, returning results and optional page content. Routes through a service that bypasses the bot protection blocking plain fetches, so use it whenever the agent needs to search or read the web.

templates.name: Ledger tools
templates.description: Read and move team work through database-enforced stages, evidence and human gates.

templates.name: Publish Artifact
templates.description: Publish a file from the agent's home directory as durable, versioned evidence — into the live Front of House conversation as a card, or from a background run with no conversation at all. Images render as cards, PDF documents receive download links, and static HTML pages open in a sandboxed preview. Every publish returns a stable public share URL anyone can open without signing in. harnesst copies the bytes without sending them through model context; publishing the same name again updates the artifact in place as a new version.

templates.name: Vercel CLI
templates.description: Run the vercel CLI against exactly one Vercel project with a project-scoped token that never enters the sandbox shell or the model's context. Every command carries the agent's written justification and is human-approved by default.
